label: Logo and brand mark
shortDescription: A focused logo competition with production-ready source files and clear usage evidence.

details.includes: Primary lockup, standalone mark, source files, export set, and usage guidance.
details.success: The identity is original, legible at required sizes, and usable in every requested format.

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Design a primary logo and standalone brand mark for {{brand}}, intended for {{audience}}. The result
should follow a {{style}} direction, remain recognizable across common product and marketing uses,
and include a short rationale connecting the design choices to the named audience.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Brand or product name: {{brand}}.
- Primary audience: {{audience}}.
- Style direction: {{style}}.
- Public references or greenfield instruction: {{brandPack}}
- Intended uses are the product and marketing placements named in the public references. No account, repository, or production access is part of this task.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Confirm the named brand, audience, intended uses, and public references are sufficient to design without requester follow-up.
- If a linked reference is inaccessible or the intended uses are unclear, do not begin the submission.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- One primary logo lockup and one standalone mark.
- Full-color, single-color, and reversed variants.
- Editable vector source plus SVG exports.
- Transparent PNG previews at 512 px, 1024 px, and 2048 px.
- A one-page usage note covering color values, clear space, and minimum practical size.
- A concise design rationale naming any third-party typeface or asset and its license.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- The supplied files include every listed lockup, variant, format, and PNG size.
- The standalone mark remains distinguishable at 16 px and the primary lockup remains legible at
  160 px wide in the submitted preview.
- Full-color, single-color, and reversed variants preserve the same recognizable construction.
- Vector files open without missing linked assets, and text is either outlined or accompanied by
  the disclosed font information.
- The rationale and license disclosure are present, with no watermark or undisclosed stock element.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- One comparison sheet showing the primary lockup and standalone mark at the acceptance sizes on
  both light and dark backgrounds.
- The editable vector source, exported SVGs, PNG previews, usage note, and license disclosure.
- A file manifest listing each artifact and its purpose.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Submit original work created for this brief; do not submit stock marks, traced artwork,
  watermarked previews, or an unchanged template.
- Any font, icon, or other third-party element must be disclosed with a license that permits the
  intended use.
- The mark must work on light and dark backgrounds and must not rely on animation to be understood.
- Keep the scope to the logo system above; naming, full brand strategy, packaging, and a multi-page
  identity system are excluded.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
Multiple workers may submit completed logo systems. The requester checks each qualifying entry
against the required variants, formats, small-size previews, originality, and rationale, then
accepts the strongest result. The task does not guarantee feedback, revisions, or payment for
unaccepted entries.

readiness.label: Public references or greenfield note
readiness.help: Link public brand references, or state that no existing identity assets apply.
readiness.placeholder: https://example.com/brand-kit or No existing assets; treat this as greenfield.
readiness.defaultValue: No existing assets; treat this as a greenfield identity.

label: Data infographic
shortDescription: Competing visual stories that turn sourced facts into one shareable infographic.

details.includes: Narrative hierarchy, source citations, editable artwork, and web-ready exports.
details.success: Every figure is accurate and the story is understandable at a glance.

tokens.label: Infographic topic
tokens.placeholder: the state of remote work in 2026

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Create a single-page data infographic about {{topic}} for {{audience}}. It should communicate one
clear narrative at a glance, support every factual claim with an accessible citation, and work as a
standalone web or social asset.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Topic: {{topic}}.
- Target audience: {{audience}}.
- Source policy: {{sourcePolicy}}
- Output format: one vertical 1080 by 1920 px artifact.
- When researching, use public primary or authoritative sources and record the title, publisher, URL, publication date, and exact figure used.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Confirm the topic, audience, source policy, and output dimensions are sufficient to create and fact-check the artifact.
- If the source policy is inaccessible or contradictory, do not begin the submission.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- One vertical infographic at 1080 by 1920 px.
- Editable source file with text and chart elements remaining editable.
- High-resolution PNG export and a web-optimized PNG or JPG under 1 MB.
- A plain-text source ledger mapping every quantitative or factual claim to its citation.
- Alt text summarizing the infographic's message and the key figures it contains.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- Every factual and quantitative claim maps to one entry in the source ledger.
- Displayed figures, units, dates, and labels match their cited sources.
- The title, primary takeaway, and reading order are clear at the submitted 1080 by 1920 px size.
- Body text and chart labels remain readable at 100 percent zoom on the final export.
- Text contrast meets WCAG AA where applicable, and each chart remains interpretable without color
  alone.
- All listed source and export files open successfully and contain no watermark.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Final and web-optimized exports.
- Editable source file.
- Source ledger with direct links and the figures used.
- Alt text plus a small screenshot or preview demonstrating the export at its intended dimensions.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not invent, extrapolate, or silently alter a figure.
- Label units, time periods, geography, sample size, and material caveats wherever they affect
  interpretation.
- Use accessible text contrast and do not rely on color alone to distinguish data series.
- Keep the artifact to one page and one primary narrative; a research report, dashboard, or
  multi-page campaign is excluded.
- Disclose any third-party visual asset and its license.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
Multiple workers may submit completed visual interpretations. The requester verifies the source
ledger and factual accuracy first, then compares qualifying entries for narrative clarity,
hierarchy, readability, accessibility, and fit for {{audience}}. The requester accepts the strongest
result; the task does not guarantee feedback, revisions, or payment for unaccepted entries.

readiness.label: Public source policy
readiness.help: Name the public source pack, or allow current primary and authoritative research.
readiness.placeholder: Use https://example.com/source-pack, or research current public primary sources.
readiness.defaultValue: Use current public primary or authoritative sources and record every citation.

label: Landing-page copy
shortDescription: Competing page narratives with complete, supportable copy from hero to final action.

details.includes: Hero, benefits, proof, objections, calls to action, and headline variants.
details.success: The page communicates a specific value proposition and clear next action.

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Write complete landing-page copy for {{product}}, speaking to {{audience}} in a {{tone}} voice. The
page should explain the product's value, support its claims, address the audience's main objections,
and lead to the primary conversion action named in the task inputs.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Product or service: {{product}}.
- Target audience: {{audience}}.
- Tone: {{tone}}.
- Public product truth pack: {{productTruthUrl}}
- Primary call to action: {{primaryCta}}.
- The truth pack is the only approved source for capabilities, proof, customer evidence, brand constraints, and reference copy. Mark an unsupported claim as `[proof required]`; do not request analytics or CMS access.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the product truth pack without signing in and confirm it supports the requested claims, audience, and call to action.
- If a required product fact is absent, mark it as a proof gap; do not invent it or request private analytics.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Hero eyebrow if useful, headline, supporting subheadline, and primary button copy.
- Three to five benefit sections with headings and body copy.
- One “how it works” or product-mechanism section.
- One trust or proof section using only substantiated inputs.
- One objection-handling or FAQ section with three to five items.
- Closing call-to-action block.
- Two additional hero-headline variants clearly separated from the primary page copy.
- A structured Markdown or document file with each page section labelled.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- Every listed page section and all three hero headline options are present.
- Each section connects a supplied product capability to a concrete reader benefit or next action.
- Every factual claim is traceable to the supplied inputs or visibly marked `[proof required]`.
- The primary conversion action remains consistent from hero to closing section.
- The copy addresses at least three distinct audience questions or objections without contradicting
  supplied product facts.
- Delivery is section-labelled, editable, and contains no unexplained placeholder other than the
  permitted `[proof required]` marker.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- The complete section-labelled copy document.
- A claim ledger listing each factual or proof-based claim and the supplied source supporting it,
  including every remaining `[proof required]` item.
- A short coverage checklist mapping the deliverable to the required page sections and primary
  conversion action.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not invent statistics, testimonials, customer logos, integrations, certifications, guarantees,
  or capabilities.
- Write for the named audience and primary action; avoid generic filler that could describe an
  unrelated product.
- Keep body sentences concise and headings scannable. Explain necessary technical terms on first
  use.
- Keep the scope to copy for one page. Positioning research, visual design, implementation, and
  multi-channel campaign assets are excluded.
- Identify any source text quoted or closely adapted from a supplied reference.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
Multiple workers may submit completed page narratives. The requester first rejects entries with
unsupported claims or missing sections, then compares qualifying submissions for audience fit,
specificity, clarity, message hierarchy, objection handling, and strength of the primary action.
The requester accepts the strongest result; the task does not guarantee feedback, revisions, or
payment for unaccepted entries.

readiness.label: Public product truth pack
readiness.help: A public page containing approved capabilities, proof, brand constraints, and reference copy.

readiness.label: Primary call to action
readiness.help: The single action the page should lead readers toward.

label: Reproducible bug fix
shortDescription: Reserve one worker to reproduce, fix, test, and explain a bounded software defect.

details.includes: Reproduction, root cause, minimal fix, regression test, and verification notes.
details.success: The issue no longer reproduces and the relevant automated checks pass.

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Fix {{issue}} in {{repository}} for {{environment}}. Keep the change focused on the documented
failure, preserve unrelated behavior, and leave a regression test that fails before the fix and
passes afterward.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Repository and pinned revision: {{repository}}.
- Observed behavior: {{issue}}.
- Affected environment: {{environment}}.
- Public reproduction contract: {{reproductionUrl}}
- Verification command: `{{testCommand}}`.
- Return the patch as the contribution format named in the reproduction contract. Repository credentials, production secrets, and private logs are outside this public task.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the repository and reproduction contract without signing in, check out the pinned revision, and reproduce the stated failure.
- If the revision, reproduction, or verification command is unavailable or inaccurate, do not claim the task.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- A focused patch, branch, or pull request against the pinned revision.
- A regression test demonstrating the reported failure and corrected behavior.
- A concise root-cause explanation naming the faulty path and why the change fixes it.
- A verification note listing commands run, results, and any relevant environment difference.
- A changed-files summary and any remaining limitation discovered within scope.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- The documented reproduction fails at the pinned revision before the patch and passes with the
  patch applied, or the worker provides evidence that the stated precondition was inaccurate.
- The new regression test exercises the failure path and passes after the fix.
- The repository's named relevant test, type, lint, and formatting commands pass.
- The patch does not include unrelated source changes or generated files outside the documented
  workflow.
- Expected behavior is observable in {{environment}} or in a documented equivalent test
  environment approved by the brief.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Patch, branch, or pull-request reference plus the exact base revision.
- Regression-test path and before/after command output.
- Relevant suite output with command names and exit status.
- Root-cause and changed-files summary, including any failed or skipped check with its reason.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not perform unrelated refactors, dependency upgrades, formatting sweeps, or behavior changes.
- Follow the repository's local contribution, test, security, and formatting instructions.
- Do not weaken, skip, or delete an existing test merely to make the suite pass.
- Do not expose secrets, production data, or private logs in committed artifacts.
- Stop and report the blocker if the supplied reproduction cannot be produced at the pinned
  revision; do not substitute a different bug.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
One worker reserves this task before starting. The requester verifies the reproduction, regression
test, relevant checks, scope of the patch, and root-cause explanation, then accepts or rejects the
submission. The task does not guarantee feedback or revisions before expiry.

readiness.label: Public reproduction contract
readiness.help: A public issue or task pack with steps, expected behavior, logs, setup, and the pinned base revision.

readiness.label: Verification command
readiness.help: The exact relevant test command available in the public repository.

label: CMS content migration
shortDescription: Reserve one operator to migrate a defined content inventory with mappings, redirects, and reconciliation.

details.includes: Inventory reconciliation, field mapping, migration, exception log, and spot checks.
details.success: Every in-scope item is migrated once and passes the agreed validation sample.

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Migrate {{contentScope}} from {{sourcePlatform}} to {{targetPlatform}} as one controlled,
reconcilable batch. Preserve the mapped content, assets, metadata, and URL intent while recording
every exception instead of silently dropping or altering content.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Source platform: {{sourcePlatform}}.
- Target schema: {{targetPlatform}}.
- Content scope: {{contentScope}}.
- Public sanitized migration pack: {{migrationPackUrl}}
- The migration pack is the source of truth for inventory, field and URL mappings, statuses, locales, exclusions, asset rules, and the import contract. This task does not include CMS login or production cutover.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the migration pack without signing in and confirm the inventory, mappings, schema, and import contract describe one complete fixed batch.
- If any required mapping or source artifact is missing, do not claim the task.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Import-ready package for {{targetPlatform}} containing every eligible record.
- Source-to-output manifest with stable source identifiers and generated destination identifiers.
- Old-to-new URL mapping and permanent-redirect file where URLs change.
- Asset manifest covering migrated, missing, transformed, and rejected files.
- Exception log with record identifier, reason, and disposition.
- Reconciliation report covering totals, statuses, locales, fields, assets, links, and redirects.
- Repeatable migration script or documented import command.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- Source totals equal migrated plus intentionally excluded plus rejected totals for every content
  type and locale.
- Every required field in the supplied mapping is populated or listed in the exception log.
- All migrated internal links and assets resolve in the agreed validation environment.
- Every changed in-scope URL has one direct destination or a documented 404/410 decision; redirect
  chains are not introduced.
- A requester-selected validation sample matches source content, formatting, metadata, and assets.
- The migration or import procedure can be repeated from the original source without undocumented
  manual changes.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Record, URL, and asset manifests plus the exception log.
- Machine-readable reconciliation totals and a human-readable summary.
- Link and redirect validation output against the packaged preview.
- Import command or migration-script instructions and the exact source/export version.
- Public preview output for the validation sample without private source content.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not overwrite, publish, delete, or mutate production content unless the brief explicitly grants
  that exact operation.
- Preserve supplied timestamps, authorship, slugs, locale, taxonomy, and SEO metadata according to
  the field mapping; report unsupported fields.
- Map each changed URL to its closest corresponding destination. Do not redirect unrelated missing
  pages to the home page.
- Do not silently omit malformed records, missing assets, or unsupported markup.
- Keep analytics, redesign, copy editing, and CMS architecture changes outside scope.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body: One worker claims this fixed migration package before starting. The requester verifies reconciliation totals, the validation sample, links, redirects, exceptions, and repeatability before accepting or rejecting the submission. Importing into a live CMS, production launch, and iterative remapping are separate work.

readiness.label: Public migration pack
readiness.help: A public sanitized export with inventory, field and URL mappings, target schema, and import contract.

label: Dataset cleanup and normalization
shortDescription: Reserve one worker to apply fixed cleanup rules and return a reproducible, reconciled dataset.

details.includes: Schema checks, normalization, deduplication, exception handling, and quality report.
details.success: The output passes every automated rule and accounts for every input record.

tokens.label: Primary cleanup goal
tokens.placeholder: normalize contacts and remove exact duplicates

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Clean and normalize {{dataset}} to produce {{outputFormat}}, with the primary goal to
{{cleanupGoal}}. Apply only the published rules, preserve provenance, and make every transformed,
deduplicated, or rejected record explainable.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Dataset and pinned version: {{dataset}}.
- Required output: {{outputFormat}}.
- Primary cleanup goal: {{cleanupGoal}}.
- Public sanitized dataset and rules pack: {{datasetRulesUrl}}
- The pack fixes the input data, target schema, normalization rules, duplicate keys and survivor policy, null policy, protected fields, fixtures, encoding, delimiter, and time-zone conventions. Personal or restricted records are outside this public task.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the dataset and rules pack without signing in and confirm its version, schema, deterministic rules, and fixtures.
- If the pack contains personal or restricted records, or a rule is undefined, do not claim the public task.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Cleaned dataset in {{outputFormat}}.
- Repeatable transformation script, query, notebook, or pipeline configuration.
- Row-level change log or stable aggregate audit where row-level output would expose restricted
  data.
- Rejected-record file containing stable identifiers and reasons.
- Validation and reconciliation report with input, output, duplicate, transformed, unchanged,
  rejected, and null counts.
- Data dictionary documenting output fields and any normalized enumerations.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- Input count reconciles to retained plus merged duplicates plus rejected records according to the
  supplied survivor policy.
- Output validates against the target schema, encoding, field types, enumerations, and required
  constraints.
- Running the supplied transformation against the pinned input produces the delivered output or an
  equivalent deterministically ordered result.
- Protected fields match their source values, and every modified field follows one published rule.
- Every rejected or ambiguous record has a stable identifier and reason.
- The validation sample and requester-provided edge cases produce the expected results.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Cleaned dataset and transformation artifact.
- Reconciliation and schema-validation output with command or execution instructions.
- Change/reject audit at the approved sensitivity level.
- Hashes or version identifiers for the source and delivered dataset.
- Results for the supplied sample and edge-case fixtures.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not infer missing facts or modify protected fields.
- Apply only the supplied normalization, null, and duplicate rules. Report ambiguous records rather
  than choosing an undocumented interpretation.
- Keep stable source identifiers so output rows and rejects can be traced to the input.
- Do not discard records silently or log sensitive raw values beyond the approved artifacts.
- Modeling, enrichment from external sources, schema design, and probabilistic entity resolution
  are outside scope unless fully specified as deterministic rules.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
One worker reserves this deterministic cleanup task. The requester verifies schema validity,
reconciliation, protected fields, rule coverage, reproducibility, and the supplied edge cases before
accepting or rejecting the submission. The task does not guarantee iterative rule discovery or a
revision round.

readiness.label: Public dataset and rules pack
readiness.help: A public sanitized dataset plus schema, normalization rules, duplicate policy, and fixtures.

label: AI workflow integration
shortDescription: Choose an architecture before one worker builds and proves a bounded AI-assisted workflow.

details.includes: Proposed architecture, model choice, risk plan, delivery milestones, and working integration.
details.success: The selected approach delivers the target workflow with observable quality and cost controls.

tokens.label: Desired outcome
tokens.placeholder: route each request with a reviewable draft response

tokens.label: Target environment
tokens.placeholder: our TypeScript service and Zendesk sandbox

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Design and implement a bounded AI-assisted integration for {{workflow}} in {{environment}}. The
integration should achieve {{outcome}} while keeping material actions reviewable, failures visible,
and the selected implementation reproducible in the named target environment.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Current workflow: {{workflow}}.
- Desired outcome: {{outcome}}.
- Target runtime: {{environment}}.
- Public integration pack: {{integrationPackUrl}}
- The pack fixes the workflow contract, mock APIs or events, sanitized fixtures, evaluation set, volume, latency and cost limits, model/tool versions, logging policy, and human approval points. Live credentials, private records, and production writes are outside this public task.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the integration pack without signing in and confirm its mocks, fixtures, evaluation set, target runtime, and approval boundaries.
- If the proposed approach requires live credentials, private records, or production writes, do not pitch it for this public task.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Working integration and source code against the public mocks or sandbox in the selected architecture.
- Versioned configuration and environment-variable schema with no embedded secrets.
- Automated tests for happy paths, malformed input, provider or tool failure, retry, timeout, duplicate events, and human rejection.
- Evaluation report against the pinned fixtures, including quality, failure, latency, and cost results.
- Architecture and data-flow summary naming models, tools, stored data, trust boundaries, and approval points.
- Setup, operation, monitoring, and rollback instructions for the public runtime.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- Every named end-to-end scenario produces its expected output or declared review state against the
  pinned evaluation set.
- Malformed input, provider failure, timeout, retry, duplicate event, and human rejection follow the
  documented safe path without an undeclared side effect.
- No secret is present in source, configuration, logs, or submitted evidence.
- Measured latency, cost, and quality satisfy the numerical limits supplied in the task, or the
  report identifies each miss without hiding it.
- A clean checkout can be configured, tested, and rolled back using the supplied instructions.
- Architecture documentation matches the delivered data flow, provider calls, storage, and approval
  boundaries.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Source revision and configuration manifest.
- Test command and unedited passing/failing summary for every required scenario.
- Evaluation report tied to the pinned dataset and model/tool versions.
- Redacted example logs demonstrating a success, a safe refusal or review handoff, and a provider or
  tool failure.
- Architecture diagram plus a setup-and-rollback walkthrough from a clean environment.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Use least-privilege access and preserve every required human approval point.
- Do not train on, retain, or send supplied data to an undeclared provider.
- Pin model, provider, library, prompt, and tool versions wherever a change could affect acceptance.
- Make retries bounded and side effects idempotent where the target interfaces permit it.
- Record refusals, low-confidence results, and tool failures rather than silently presenting them as
  successful output.
- General platform redesign, unrestricted autonomous action, model training, and production rollout
  are excluded unless the published inputs explicitly specify them.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
Each pitch should state the proposed architecture and data flow, model/tool rationale, evaluation
method, security and failure risks, milestones, estimated duration, and one relevant prior artifact
or result. It may include a small pseudocode or interface example, but must not include the finished
integration. The requester selects the approach that best fits the published environment,
constraints, evaluation method, and risk controls, then reviews the selected worker's final
deliverables against the criteria above.

readiness.label: Public integration pack
readiness.help: A public repository or specification with mock APIs, sanitized fixtures, evaluation data, and runtime constraints.

label: UX/UI redesign
shortDescription: Compare product diagnoses and design approaches before one worker redesigns a complete flow.

details.includes: Problem framing, proposed direction, key flows, high-fidelity screens, and handoff notes.
details.success: The selected solution resolves the priority user problem and is ready for implementation.

tokens.label: Flow to redesign
tokens.placeholder: finding and resolving an escalated ticket

tokens.label: Primary user
tokens.placeholder: support leads working across large queues

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Redesign {{flow}} in {{product}} for {{audience}}. The result should resolve the documented user
problem, cover the complete interaction rather than an isolated attractive screen, and provide
editable, accessible, implementation-ready design specifications.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Product or surface: {{product}}.
- Flow: {{flow}}.
- Primary user: {{audience}}.
- Public current-state and evidence pack: {{designContextUrl}}
- The pack fixes the current screens or build, observed evidence, brand and component guidance, platforms, breakpoints, content constraints, and preserved behaviors. Distinguish observed evidence from requester assumptions; private analytics and a restricted test environment are outside this task.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the design context without signing in and confirm the current flow, evidence, platform constraints, and required states are visible.
- If the evidence is absent, treat requester beliefs as assumptions in the pitch; do not imply private analytics will arrive later.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Current-state diagnosis and a concise prioritized problem statement.
- End-to-end user flow covering entry, core path, completion, and recovery.
- High-fidelity screens for every agreed step at each supplied breakpoint.
- Loading, empty, error, validation, disabled, permission, and success states that can occur in the
  named flow.
- Component and interaction annotations covering behavior, content, keyboard order, focus, and
  responsive changes.
- Clickable prototype for the critical path, editable source files, and a handoff manifest linking
  screens to existing or proposed components.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- The delivered screen-and-state matrix contains every agreed flow step, breakpoint, and applicable
  loading, empty, error, permission, validation, disabled, and success state.
- The prototype completes the critical path and at least one named recovery path without a dead end.
- Annotations specify keyboard order, focus behavior, labels, responsive behavior, and component
  reuse or additions for each interactive screen.
- Text and UI component contrast meet WCAG AA against the supplied palette, with exceptions named
  and measured rather than hidden.
- Editable source files open without missing assets, and every handoff link resolves to the matching
  screen or component note.
- The diagnosis distinguishes supplied evidence, reasonable inference, and open research questions.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Editable design source, prototype link, and export manifest.
- Flow diagram and screen-and-state coverage matrix.
- Accessibility checklist with contrast measurements and keyboard/focus notes.
- Component reuse/addition inventory and a walkthrough of the critical and recovery paths.
- A trace from each prioritized problem to the screen, interaction, or open question that addresses it.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Preserve the published brand and platform constraints unless a deviation is explicitly explained.
- Reuse supplied design-system components where they meet the need; identify proposed additions or
  variants rather than silently forking them.
- Support keyboard operation, visible focus, meaningful labels, reduced motion where applicable,
  and WCAG AA contrast for supplied colors and states.
- Do not rely on color alone for status or remove a required workflow capability to simplify a mock.
- Production frontend implementation, new user research, a full product redesign, and unrelated
  flows are excluded unless explicitly included in the published task.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
Each pitch should provide a concise diagnosis, design principles, evidence and assumptions, proposed
process and artifacts, accessibility approach, milestones, estimated duration, and representative
prior work. A pitch may show a rough flow fragment or explain one design principle, but must not
contain the finished screens or full redesign. The requester selects the strongest evidence-aware,
feasible approach, then evaluates the selected worker's final coverage, interaction coherence,
accessibility, editability, and implementation handoff.

readiness.label: Public design context
readiness.help: A public build or screenshot pack with current states, evidence, design constraints, and target breakpoints.

label: Go-to-market launch plan
shortDescription: Select an audience and channel thesis before one strategist builds an evidence-led launch plan.

details.success: The plan gives the team a specific, testable route to the target audience.

Create an evidence-led go-to-market launch plan for {{product}}, prioritizing {{audience}}, with the

brief.heading: Public inputs

- Priority audience: {{audience}}.
- Launch goal: {{launchGoal}}.

brief.body:
- Open the launch pack without signing in and confirm it states the approved facts, launch constraints, budget, capacity, and measurement sources.
- If execution would require a CRM, customer list, ad account, or private analytics, keep that work outside this planning pitch.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Audience definition, priority segment rationale, buying context, and key objections.
- Positioning statement, message hierarchy, proof mapping, and prohibited or unsupported claims.
- Channel plan with role, audience, activity, owner, timing, budget, dependencies, and rationale for
  each recommended channel.
- Launch calendar covering preparation, launch, and follow-through.
- Two to four campaign concepts with channel, audience, message, call to action, and required asset
  outline; finished campaign production is not included.
- Measurement framework connecting the launch goal to leading and outcome indicators, source,
  cadence, decision threshold, and owner.
- Prioritized next actions, material risks, assumptions, and contingency triggers.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- Every activity maps to a priority audience, message, launch phase, owner, timing, cost, and measure.
- Planned external spend does not exceed the supplied budget, and all material dependencies are named.
- Every factual market, customer, competitor, and performance claim maps to a supplied or cited source;
  unsupported statements are labelled as hypotheses or gaps.
- The calendar fits the supplied launch date and team capacity, with prerequisite and fallback paths.
- The measurement framework defines the formula or event source, cadence, owner, and action threshold
  for each primary measure.
- Campaign concepts remain consistent with the approved product truth, proof, brand, legal constraints,
  and call to action.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Final plan in an editable document or structured Markdown file.
- Source ledger mapping claims and decisions to supplied or discovered evidence.
- Channel-and-budget table whose totals reconcile to the stated budget.
- Launch calendar, ownership matrix, measurement table, and execution checklist.
- Assumption, risk, and evidence-gap register with proposed validation or contingency action.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not invent customer quotes, market figures, product capabilities, certifications, performance
  history, or legal claims. Mark a missing proof point as a gap.
- Keep total planned spend within the supplied budget and distinguish media spend, tools, production,
  and internal effort where the inputs permit it.
- Recommend only channels the supplied geography, timing, team, consent, and access constraints can
  support; explain any proposed prerequisite.
- Separate sourced facts, requester assumptions, strategist inferences, and hypotheses to test.
- Ad buying, outreach execution, asset production, sales operations, and product changes are outside
  scope unless expressly added to the published task.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
Each pitch should state its audience thesis, positioning hypothesis, channel-selection method,
research gaps, success-measure approach, major risks, milestones, estimated duration, and comparable
prior work. It may include a short illustrative positioning angle, but must not deliver the completed
strategy, channel plan, or launch calendar before selection. The requester selects the proposal
whose reasoning, evidence plan, feasibility, and measurement approach best fit the published inputs,
then reviews the selected worker's completed plan against the criteria above.

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Optimize the prompt or agent configuration for {{task}} using {{model}} and {{evaluationSet}}. The
winning eligible artifact maximizes held-out pass rate without changing the pinned evaluator,
exceeding the supplied cost or latency gates, or leaking held-out examples.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Task: {{task}}.
- Model and version: {{model}}.
- Evaluation set and harness: {{evaluationSet}}.
- Public benchmark pack: {{benchmarkPackUrl}}
- The pack fixes the baseline artifact and score, public development set, evaluator and rubric, run command, allowed context and tools, generation parameters, run count, aggregation, token prices, latency environment, eligibility gates, and sealed held-out procedure. Held-out examples, labels, and secrets are never worker inputs.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the benchmark pack without signing in and reproduce the baseline with the pinned public development harness.
- Confirm the requester or evaluator can run the sealed held-out set; if held-out labels are exposed or the proof path is undefined, do not enter.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Complete optimized prompt, agent configuration, and any allowed tool definitions or deterministic
  preprocessing needed to run it.
- Machine-readable configuration pinning model, parameters, tool and dependency versions.
- Runnable development-evaluation command and environment setup.
- Raw development results and authorized held-out result artifact.
- Method summary describing changes, experiments, failure analysis, and discarded approaches.
- Canonical proof package with primary score, gates, tie-breakers, artifact revision, and caveats.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- The authorized held-out runner produces a pass rate above the published baseline using the pinned
  model, evaluator, dataset version, run count, and aggregation rule.
- `metricValue` equals `round(passRate * 10000)` and lies between 0 and 10000 inclusive.
- Median token cost and p95 latency meet their published gates, and every required tool or format
  check passes.
- A clean development run using the supplied command reproduces the reported development score
  within the task's declared stochastic tolerance.
- The submitted artifact is complete, contains no per-record answer map or held-out identifier
  branch, and matches the revision named in the proof.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Optimized artifact and immutable revision.
- Canonical proof package with `metricValue` encoded in basis points.
- Raw per-example or aggregate outputs at the visibility level permitted by the held-out policy,
  including failures rather than only successful cases.
- Harness output naming model snapshot, evaluator, dataset hash, generation parameters, token use,
  latency, run count, and final aggregation.
- Baseline comparison and reproduction command from a clean environment.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not change the pinned model, evaluator, task inputs, reference answers, run count, sampling
  configuration, tool allowance, or score aggregation unless the brief explicitly marks it variable.
- Do not inspect, reconstruct, memorize, encode, or manually special-case sealed held-out examples or
  labels. Do not key outputs to record IDs, order, hashes, or other evaluation-set fingerprints.
- The submitted artifact must handle every evaluation record; omit neither failures nor low scores.
- Stay within the published median token-cost and p95 latency gates, using the supplied calculation.
- Disclose every external prompt, dataset, model, tool, and code dependency and its version.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
The requester first rejects entries that fail leakage review, artifact completeness, model or tool
pinning, format checks, cost, latency, or reproducibility. Among eligible entries, the highest
held-out pass-rate basis points wins. Ties compare lower median token cost, then lower p95 latency,
then the earlier onchain proof submission. These rules are requester-applied; Taskmarket records the
claim but does not execute them automatically.

modeDefaults.metricDescription: Held-out pass rate in basis points (0-10000); higher is better.
modeDefaults.metricTarget: Exceed the published baseline; tie-break lower median token cost, then lower p95 latency.

brief.heading: Outcome
brief.body:
Reduce p95 response latency for {{endpoint}} in {{repository}} under {{loadProfile}}. The winning
eligible change has the lowest independently reproduced p95 latency while preserving response
correctness, throughput, reliability, and the fixed resource and dependency boundaries.

brief.heading: Public inputs
brief.body:
- Endpoint or operation: {{endpoint}}.
- Repository and revision: {{repository}}.
- Load profile: {{loadProfile}}.
- Public reproducible benchmark pack: {{benchmarkPackUrl}}
- The pack fixes the benchmark script, request corpus and seed, container digest, hardware profile, dependency fixtures, warm-up and cache policy, run duration and count, baseline output, correctness suite, resource ceilings, and every numerical gate. Production infrastructure and credentials are outside this benchmark.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the benchmark pack without signing in and reproduce its baseline inside the pinned container and fixed fixtures.
- If scoring depends on production infrastructure, credentials, or an unspecified resource, do not enter the benchmark.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:
- Source and configuration change as a reviewable patch or repository revision.
- Tests covering the changed behavior and any newly exposed race, cache, or failure path.
- Reproducible benchmark environment and exact baseline/candidate commands.
- Raw result files for all required baseline and candidate runs.
- Before/after report covering p50, p95, p99, throughput, error rate, CPU, memory, network, and
  dependency calls or time where the harness exposes them.
- Canonical proof package with the candidate p95 in whole microseconds, gates, tie-breakers, artifact
  revision, run order, and caveats.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- At least the published number of clean candidate runs complete under the pinned image, hardware,
  fixtures, load script, run duration, concurrency, and run-order policy.
- `metricValue` is the aggregation rule's candidate p95 converted to whole microseconds with no
  decimal or unit ambiguity, and it is lower than the published baseline value.
- The correctness suite passes, error rate does not exceed its gate, minimum throughput is met, and
  CPU, memory, network, storage, and dependency-service measurements stay within their ceilings.
- Raw outputs include all scheduled iterations and errors, and recomputing the percentile from them
  yields the claimed value under the supplied percentile method.
- A clean checkout of the named revision builds, tests, and runs with the supplied commands.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Source revision or patch and automated test output.
- Canonical proof package plus immutable raw output from every baseline and candidate score run.
- Environment manifest naming image digest, hardware, dependency versions, load-script revision,
  request-corpus hash, run order, warm-up, and cache state.
- Recalculation command for p95 and each gate.
- Before/after report and a short explanation of the optimization and its tradeoffs.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Preserve response semantics and pass the complete pinned correctness suite.
- Do not remove work, narrow the request corpus, lower concurrency or duration, skip slow responses,
  hide errors, precompute fixture-specific answers, or move measured work outside the timed boundary.
- Follow the supplied warm-up, connection reuse, cache, database state, rate-limit, and run-order
  policy for both baseline and candidate.
- Stay within the published CPU, memory, network, storage, and downstream-service ceilings. Disclose
  any capacity or topology change; an undeclared resource increase makes the entry ineligible.
- Exclude debugger, profiler, and unrelated background-load runs from score runs, but retain them as
  supporting diagnostic evidence where useful.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
The requester first excludes entries that fail correctness, error rate, throughput, resource,
environment, completeness, anti-shortcut, or reproduction checks. Among eligible entries, the
lowest p95 microseconds wins. Ties compare lower median latency, then lower peak memory, then the
earlier onchain proof submission. The protocol records the integer claim and proof commitment but
does not calculate a percentile or enforce a gate.

modeDefaults.metricDescription: p95 response latency in whole microseconds under the pinned load profile; lower is better.
modeDefaults.metricTarget: Beat the published baseline while passing correctness, error-rate, throughput, and resource gates.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:

- Confirm the requester or evaluator runs the sealed corpus; if private held-out documents must be downloaded by workers, do not enter.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:

- Machine-readable outputs for the development set and the authorized held-out result.
- Schema validator and exact scoring command.
- Tests for required, optional, repeated, missing, malformed, and unsupported fields plus unreadable

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- The authorized held-out runner reports macro field-level F1 above the published baseline using the
  pinned corpus, schema, normalization rules, scorer, and averaging behavior.
- `metricValue` equals `round(macroF1 * 10000)` and lies between 0 and 10000 inclusive.
- Every input has one output disposition, schema-valid outputs meet the required validity rate, and
  failures remain included under the scorer's declared policy.
- Per-record cost and p95 latency meet the published gates, and model/tool versions match the
  submitted configuration.
- A clean run against the labelled development set reproduces the reported development metric and
  exact-match count using the supplied command.
- Leakage review finds no record-specific answer map, held-out label, or evaluation-set fingerprint.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Extractor revision, configuration, lockfile, and setup instructions.
- Canonical proof package with primary score encoded in basis points.
- Raw scorer and schema-validator output naming corpus, schema, scorer, model/tool, and environment
  versions, with aggregate counts that include every record.
- Field-level precision, recall, F1, support, exact-match, cost, latency, and failure-category report.
- Immutable development output and authorized held-out result at the permitted visibility level.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Do not inspect or reconstruct held-out labels, manually map held-out record IDs to outputs, encode
  answers from file names or ordering, or omit difficult records.
- Do not alter the corpus, schema, normalization, scorer, macro averaging, or failure treatment.
- Produce one declared output for every input, including an explicit failure object where the schema
  permits it; never silently drop a failed document from scoring.
- Use only the allowed models, services, external data, and tools, pinned to the versions required by
  the brief. Disclose every dependency and per-record external call.
- Stay within the published per-record cost and p95 latency gates.

brief.heading: How selection works
brief.body:
The requester first excludes entries that fail schema validity, corpus completeness, leakage,
allowed-tool, cost, latency, artifact, or reproduction checks. Among eligible entries, the highest
macro field-level F1 basis points wins. Ties compare higher record exact-match basis points, then
lower per-record cost in the task's declared integer unit, then lower p95 latency, then the earlier
onchain proof submission. Taskmarket does not execute the scorer or enforce this ordering.

modeDefaults.metricDescription: Macro field-level F1 in basis points (0-10000) on held-out records; higher is better.
modeDefaults.metricTarget: Exceed the published baseline; tie-break record exact match, then lower cost, then lower p95 latency.

brief.heading: Readiness gate
brief.body:
- Open the complete batch without signing in and confirm its item count, taxonomy, decision rules, scorer, and output format.
- Bid only if the entire fixed file-based batch can be completed at the offered price; do not assume tool credentials or extra examples will arrive later.

brief.heading: Deliverables
brief.body:

- Schema-valid export ready for the public importer or evaluator.
- Ambiguity and abstention log with item identifier, rule considered, and reason.
- Quality report containing counts by label, unlabeled and multi-label counts, QC score, and systematic issues.

brief.heading: Acceptance
brief.body:
- The output contains exactly one permitted disposition for every one of the {{itemCount}} stable
  identifiers, with no unknown, duplicate, added, or silently missing item.
- The supplied schema and importer validate the complete export without error.
- The published QC scorer reaches or exceeds its numerical threshold on the fixed sample under the
  declared tie, abstention, and multi-label rules.
- Every abstained, ambiguous, or rejected record appears in the log with an allowed reason.
- Label counts reconcile to total item count under the published multi-label accounting rule.
- Submitted files and evidence contain no prohibited raw values or credential material.

brief.heading: Evidence
brief.body:
- Final label export and content hash or immutable manifest.
- Schema/importer command with complete output.
- QC scorer command and unedited aggregate result against the pinned sample.
- Reconciliation table for total, labelled, multi-labelled, abstained, ambiguous, and rejected items.
- Ambiguity log and data-handling attestation naming the execution environment without exposing data.

brief.heading: Boundaries
brief.body:
- Apply only the published taxonomy and decision rules; do not invent labels or silently reinterpret
  a class.
- Do not guess when the abstention or escalation rule applies, and do not omit difficult items.
- Do not use automated, model-generated, or subcontracted labels unless the task explicitly permits
  that method and applies the same QC requirements to it.
- Keep source data inside the approved environment and do not reproduce restricted content in logs,
  screenshots, or public evidence.
- Model training, taxonomy redesign, active-learning strategy, and sourcing additional records are
  outside this fixed batch.

brief.heading: How selection works
